name: partylayer
description: PartyLayer - CIP-0103 compliant wallet SDK for Canton Network
author: PartyLayer Contributors

scripts.gate: pnpm gate:no-private-keys && pnpm gate:lockfile && pnpm gate:workspace-protocol && pnpm gate:build && pnpm gate:validate-publish && pnpm gate:size && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm gate:test && pnpm gate:test-skips && pnpm gate:conformance && pnpm gate:api && pnpm gate:consistency && pnpm gate:docs-drift && pnpm gate:registry && pnpm gate:wallet-marks && pnpm gate:readme && pnpm gate:templates && pnpm gate:release-changeset && pnpm gate:discovery-demos && pnpm gate:adapters-closed && pnpm gate:package-contents && pnpm gate:verify-e2e
scripts.//gate:lockfile: Fails when a package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml disagree, exactly as Vercel does with --frozen-lockfile (the CI default). A plain local pnpm install regenerates the lockfile silently, so drift never surfaced locally; this stage reproduces the CI install so the same failure is caught before it ships. It runs first because a stale lockfile invalidates every stage after it, and it is a sub-second no-op resolve once deps are already installed.
scripts.//gate:no-private-keys: This repository is public. Fails if private key material is tracked. Runs FIRST in the chain: it is the cheapest check and the most expensive failure to discover late.
scripts.//gate:workspace-protocol: The CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml, 'Check workspace protocols') runs this and the gate did not, so a green local gate did not predict a green CI: a workspace:* dependency passed every gate stage and failed CI. Delegates to lint:workspace-protocol so the two can never diverge. Runs second, right after the lockfile, because it is a sub-second read of every package.json and a wrong protocol invalidates what the later publish and build stages are checking.
scripts.//gate:build: Delegates to `build`, so the gate runs the EXACT command a deploy runs and the two can never diverge. It previously filtered to @partylayer/*, which structurally could not see a break outside that scope: examples/telemetry-adapters typechecked a test file and broke the root build for every project after it, invisibly to this gate. Serial (--workspace-concurrency=1, set in `build`): the parallel -r build can start a dependent package (e.g. testing) before a workspace dep (session) has flushed its .d.ts, an intermittent DTS-resolution race; serial enforces topological order deterministically.
scripts.//gate:validate-publish: The CI job ('Validate publish coherence') runs this and the gate did not. It checks that the published @partylayer/* set is internally coherent, which is exactly the class of break that only shows up after a release. Delegates to validate:publish so the gate runs the same command CI does.
scripts.release: pnpm build && node scripts/copy-license.mjs && changeset publish
scripts.//gate:adapters-closed: packages/adapters is closed to new wallets: a wallet integrates through the generic Path A (announce) or Path B (official ProviderAdapter) and ships no PartyLayer-specific code. The packages there predate those paths. A contributor reading the tree before the docs site could infer that adding another package is the expected route, which means building something the project does not need and finding out late, so the wrong path fails here in seconds with the right path printed. The allowlist in the check is frozen; editing it is the deliberate escape hatch and must be justified in the pull request.
scripts.//gate:package-contents: Packs every publishable package and asserts what it actually ships: every target named in exports/main/module/types/bin exists in the tarball, LICENSE and README are present, and no source, tests, tsconfig or tsbuildinfo are included. A tarball is the only thing a consumer sees and the one artifact that cannot be corrected after publish, and neither class of defect is visible in source review or in a build. It packs with pnpm, not npm, so the workspace protocol is rewritten as it will be at publish, and it runs copy-license first because packages/*/LICENSE is generated and gitignored.
scripts.//gate:verify-e2e: The CI job ('Run Full Verification Pipeline') runs this and the gate did not. Runs LAST: it is the slowest stage and it re-runs install and build internally, so every cheaper check should have failed first. Needs Playwright chromium; install once with `pnpm --filter partylayer-demo exec playwright install --with-deps chromium`. CI=true matches the CI environment, under which the script skips the browser-dependent adapter conformance checks exactly as it does in CI. Writes a report under artifacts/, which is gitignored.
scripts.//gate:_ci-steps-deliberately-not-in-the: One CI step is intentionally absent. ci.yml's 'Verify Registry Signatures' runs registry:verify for each channel, but every one of its guards is a file-existence test and none of those files exist in the repo: registry/v1/stable/registry.sig, registry/v1/beta/registry.sig and registry/keys/dev.pub are all absent, so the step is a no-op in CI as well. Adding it to the gate would add a stage that verifies nothing. If signing is ever turned on and those files start shipping, add `pnpm gate:registry-signatures` wrapping registry:verify to the chain at that time, or this gap becomes real. The remaining ci.yml entries that are not gate stages are environment setup (checkout, pnpm/node setup, Playwright browser install) and artifact upload, none of which are checks.
